videos.title: It's not you. Bad doors are everywhere.
videos.why: Vox and 99% Invisible visit Don Norman to explain why a door that needs a 'push' sign has failed; watch for the handles that invite pulling, then hunt for the screen version, a button that looks like plain text.

videos.title: Flat UI Elements Lack Clickability Clues and Cause Confusion
videos.why: Kate Moran presents eyetracking studies where people hesitated over flat designs with weak signifiers; note which missing clues (shape, colour, underline) caused the extra searching.

podcasts.episode: Auditory Icons: Credit card beeps to driverless car melodies
podcasts.why: What separates a good device sound from a bad one, from card reader beeps to alert tones; listen to it as the audio version of the feedback a button should give on screen.

reads.title: Beyond Blue Links: Making Clickable Elements Recognizable
reads.why: The visual signals that tell people something can be clicked or tapped; use it as a checklist against the buttons and links in your own app.

reads.title: Apple’s products are getting harder to use because they ignore the principles of design.
reads.why: Norman's short complaint about hidden gestures, missing feedback, no undo and unlabelled icons; read it for the vocabulary, then spot the same problems in apps you use daily.

reads.title: Visibility of System Status
reads.why: The first of Nielsen's usability heuristics, which is about feedback; the examples show what to add when your app goes quiet after someone clicks.
